RagShortTexts: Milan anchored Lombardy's Po Valley agriculture and commanded Europe's finest armor workshops.

Variants.Content: Milan sat at the heart of Lombardy, on the fertile Po plain, and it commanded the road networks linking the Alpine passes with the river valleys. Its armourers were among the best in Europe. Guild workshops drew iron from the Alps and worked it with water-powered trip-hammers, producing mail and the newer transitional plates that combined riveted rings with solid pieces. Other courts came to Milan when they needed harness in quantity. Civic politics fed the trade, because the Torriani and Visconti houses fought for control of the city and each faction armed its followers with the best mail it could buy. Canal and irrigation works across the plain kept grain and fodder moving toward the markets, so the commune could feed its citizens through a long war.

In the armorers' quarter, watermills drive deafening trip-hammers. Milanese masters understand biomechanics intimately, articulating overlapping plates so seamlessly that harness feels like a second skin.

Going into battle in Milanese mail gives a soldier real confidence, because the links are close and the plates sit well on the body. Heavy crossbow quarrels glance off the cold-worked iron. Armour does not save a man who breaks ranks, though, so keep your shield up and your place in the line.
